Tech Insider: ChatGPT Go vs Plus vs Pro

caption:
Gemini and ChatGPT both have a free plan, a cheap tier, a $20 tier and plans that reach $200 or more.
Gemini bundles storage, Gmail and Docs. ChatGPT bundles projects, custom GPTs and Codex.
Here is which one fits which job.

Which one do you use more, Gemini or ChatGPT?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

threads_text: Gemini vs ChatGPT is mostly a question of what else you use. Google AI Pro comes with 5 TB of storage and Gemini inside Gmail and Docs; ChatGPT Plus gives you projects, custom GPTs and Codex for $20. Which one do you actually open every day?

slides.headline: Gemini vs ChatGPT: *which one to use* for what

slides.heading: 1. Both start *free*
paras: Gemini Free includes image editing, Deep Research, Gemini Live and Canvas.

slides.heading: 2. Gemini comes with *storage*

If you already live in Google's apps, that bundle is hard to beat.

There is no yearly discount on personal ChatGPT plans.

ChatGPT Pro comes at $100, $200 or $500 a month.

site_article.headline: Gemini vs ChatGPT: which AI assistant to use for what, plans compared
site_article.dek: Both have a free plan, a $20 tier and plans that climb to $200 or more. Gemini sells itself as part of Google's apps, ChatGPT as a workspace of its own.
site_article.summary: Gemini and ChatGPT cost about the same at every level, but they bundle different things. Google AI plans add storage and Gemini inside Gmail and Docs; ChatGPT plans add projects, custom GPTs and the Codex coding agent.
site_article.seo_title: Gemini vs ChatGPT: which AI assistant to use, plans compared
site_article.seo_description: Gemini vs ChatGPT compared plan by plan: what the free tiers include, what $20 gets you, the $100 to $500 plans, and which one fits which kind of work.
site_article.answer_summary: Pick Gemini if you already use Gmail, Docs and Google Drive, since Google AI Pro adds Gemini inside those apps plus 5 TB of storage. Pick ChatGPT if you want one standalone workspace with projects, custom GPTs and Codex for $20 a month.

paragraphs.text: Gemini vs ChatGPT is the other big question people ask before paying for an AI assistant. Both have a free plan, a cheaper tier below $20, a main plan around $20 a month and plans for heavy users that cost $100 or more. What you get at each level is different, and so is the thinking behind it.

This guide compares what each plan includes according to Google's own plan page and announcement, and recent plan comparisons for ChatGPT. It does not rank which model is smarter, because that changes with every release. Prices can differ by country, and both companies change their plans often, so check the price at checkout.
Gemini vs ChatGPT: the free plans

Google's plan page says the free Gemini app includes a Flash-Lite model, image generation and editing, Deep Research, Gemini Live voice chat, Canvas and Skills. A free Google Account also gets limited use of Nano Banana Pro in Google Flow, the Gemini Notebook research assistant and 15 GB of storage across Gmail, Drive and Photos.

ChatGPT Free includes limited file uploads, image creation, voice, deep research, memory and the Codex coding agent, according to Tech Insider's November 2026 plan breakdown. Krater notes that free limits get tighter at busy times.
Both free plans are good enough to test with your own work. Do that before you pay, because the plan pages describe features, not how well each model handles your kind of task.
The $20 tier: Google AI Pro vs ChatGPT Plus

Google AI Pro adds Gemini 4 Argon, Google's Pro model, alongside Gemini 4 Hydrogen, with four times the free usage limits and video generation. It also brings Gemini into Gmail and Docs, 1,000 Google Flow credits, 5 TB of storage and the YouTube Premium Lite plan, according to Google's plan page. Digital Applied listed the price at $19.99 a month in May 2026.

ChatGPT Plus costs $20 a month. It adds OpenAI's flagship GPT models, projects, custom GPTs, Sites, expanded deep research and more Codex use. Personal ChatGPT plans are billed month to month, with no annual discount.

The two $20 plans are built for different people. Google AI Pro is the better deal if you already pay for Google storage or spend your day in Gmail and Docs. ChatGPT Plus is the better pick if you want one place to organize long projects, build custom GPTs or hand coding work to Codex.
The cheaper tiers

Google AI Plus sits below Pro. Google's plan page says it adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen, double the free usage limits, video generation, 200 Flow credits and Gemini in Gmail. Digital Applied listed it at $7.99 a month in May 2026.
ChatGPT Go also sits below Plus. It gives more messages, uploads, images and memory than Free, and Krater notes that it may show ads. Its price differs by country.
Plans for heavy users

Google announced at I/O on May 19, 2026 that AI Ultra now comes in two tiers: $100 a month with five times the Pro usage limits, and $200 a month, cut from $250, with twenty times the Pro limits. Both include YouTube Premium, and the $200 tier adds Project Genie, built on Google's Genie 3 world model.
ChatGPT Pro comes at $100, $200 and $500 a month. All three add higher usage and OpenAI's Pro models, and only the $500 plan includes Ultrafast mode, according to Krater and Tech Insider.

Google also changed how limits work. The Gemini app moved from daily prompt caps to limits based on how much computing a request uses. They refresh every five hours until a weekly cap is reached, and when you hit the cap on the top model, Gemini moves you to a smaller one.
How to decide in one afternoon

paragraphs.title: 1. Pick three real tasks
paragraphs.text: Choose three things you did this week: an email you had to write, a document you had to summarize and a question you had to research. Use the same three in both apps.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: Summarize a document
paragraphs.text: Summarize the attached document in five bullet points. Then list three questions it leaves unanswered, and quote the sentence each question comes from.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Research with sources
paragraphs.text: Research [topic] and give me a one page brief. Cite a source for every claim and tell me which claims you are least sure about.

paragraphs.title: 2. Check what each one got wrong
paragraphs.text: Open the sources each app cites and check two or three claims. The app that makes fewer mistakes on your topic is the one to pay for.

paragraphs.title: 3. Count the apps you already use
paragraphs.text: If Gmail, Docs and Drive are open all day, the Google plan adds value outside the chat window. If most of your AI use happens in one chat window, ChatGPT's projects and custom GPTs matter more.
Do not pay for both at once. Start with one month of the plan that fits your apps, and switch if it keeps failing on your real tasks.
